# Encounters with Flariel's Reavers

*Page PDF 15*

THE CORSAIRS OF CAPTAIN FL ARIEL 

## **Encounters with Flariel’s Reavers**
Encounters with Captain Flariel and his Elves need not descend into a fight, though violence lurks beneath the surface. If the Characters are at sea, taking on the whole crew of the _Raptor’s Talon_ is a serious challenge — though with resourceful thinking and sufficient firepower, they may triumph. On land, the party will likely encounter smaller groups of Flariel’s Reavers, opening up possibilities for social interaction and even alliance — although this will be temporary and almost inevitably end in treachery. If High Elves are present, the likelihood of a nonviolent encounter is very small, as captured Asur command a high price back in Naggaroth. 

Alternatively, the party could be captured by the Reavers and forced to become oarsmen. An encounter with Cynwra and the other captives could lead to an adventure in which they plot to overcome their cruel masters before they are shipped to Naggaroth. 

## **The Relic Hunters**
## **Easy Encounter**
This event can happen in any coastal location, particularly places with ancient Elven ruins or legends of sunken settlements. Rakaria leads a small party searching for an Elven site she believes is somewhere hereabouts. The group keep a low profile, although they will meet the locals with violence if necessary. 

If the Characters attack, Rakaria engages them with magic as the corsairs charge in firing their crossbow pistols. If matters become desperate, they will retreat to the _Raptor’s Talon_ under cover of an _Illusion_ spell. 

If the Characters offer advice or try to make a bargain, Rakaria assents, providing it leads to an Elven site. The nature of this site is up to the GM to determine — it could be a crumbling tower deep in the forest, the foundations of a shore fort projecting from sand dunes, or a line of monoliths, overgrown with moss. 

The site is occupied by a band of Beastmen (or similar) who outnumber Rakaria and her entourage. The sorceress offers to increase payment by 5 GCs if the party help clear the ruin. If Rakaria secures the site, she has no further use for the party and would rather they didn’t communicate the encounter to others. At the climax of any battle, she attempts to turn the tables on the party and wipe them out along with the Beastmen. 

This encounter should not be too difficult for most parties, as they should outnumber Rakaria and her group. However — they need to have their wits about them, as a Dark Elf sorceress is far more cunning than your average adversary. 

Rakaria’s party consists of: 

- Rakaria Dran. 

- Two Dark Elf Corsairs, armed with crossbow pistols and two swords. 

- Khana, Dark Elf Crew, armed with a sword. She will stay close to Rakaria in the event of a fight. 

Rakaria ventures forth at twilight, using _Night Vision_ to make stealth easier. They scout the land, with Rakaria invoking minor magical cantrips to ascertain their position and identify recognisable landmarks from the ancient Elven texts. 

If the party meet Rakaria’s expedition, the sorceress is too intelligent to default to violence — she needs information to navigate these strange shores. While her corsair guards move into a defensive position, Rakaria gestures for them to stand down and issues a curt instruction to them in the _Druhir_ dialect of Elthárin. 

If the party look particularly weak or include any High Elf Characters, she tries to capture them, hoping to interrogate them for the whereabouts of the Elven ruins. Otherwise, she attempts to parley. Rakaria hails the party in heavily-accented Reikspiel (or the local language) and asks whether they know of any landmarks hereabouts, specifically those built by ‘her kinfolk’. In exchange, she can offer them payment — a pouch of 25 gold coins from diverse nations of the Known World.
